name: Andy Byrne
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Clari (merged with Salesloft in Dec 2025; Steve Cox named CEO of combined company). Current post-merger role not publicly confirmed.
profile: Silicon Valley sales/product executive who co-founded revenue-forecasting SaaS company Clari in 2013 with Venkat Rangan and led it as CEO to a ~$3B valuation. Earlier founded Timestock and was on the founding exec team at Clearwell Systems (acquired by Symantec). Clari merged with Vista-backed Salesloft, a deal announced Aug 2025 and closed Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: Clari and Salesloft announced a 'merger of equals' in August 2025 to create an AI revenue platform; Byrne was originally slated to lead the combined company.
deep_cut_fact: Grew up around Mountain View, where his father leased office space to tech startups; he says dinner-table stories about companies like Fairchild Semiconductor made him love 'the idea that you could create something from nothing.' He practices Qi Gong and has a family motto 'DPA' (Dream. Plan. Act.).
notes: Post-merger role unclear (Steve Cox became CEO at close per Business Wire). No published press email found on Salesloft/Clari newsrooms; best route likely LinkedIn or via Sequoia network. TechCrunch 2014 quoted him: Clari was his 'company number-four with Sequoia.'

name: David Sehyuk Park
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Information Officer, Moloco (Redwood City, CA)
profile: Korean-born engineer who co-founded machine-learning ad-tech company Moloco in 2013 with CEO Ikkjin Ahn after ~6 years at Oracle on cloud/virtualization (Nimbula) teams. As CIO he leads Moloco's largest global team of ML engineers, data scientists and data engineers behind its ML ad platform. BS in CS from Seoul National University; graduate studies at Stanford.
interesting_fact: Before Oracle he did graduate work at Stanford in CS/machine learning; Moloco grew into a ~$2B-valued ML performance-advertising company serving mobile apps, retail media and streaming.
deep_cut_fact: Per co-founder Ikkjin Ahn (2021 ZDNet Korea interview), Park did his master's under Andrew Ng at Stanford, was Ahn's junior by three years in SNU computer science, swept International Olympiad in Informatics medals as a youth, and had tried founding startups several times before Moloco.
notes: Low public profile; Ahn is the main spokesperson. Moloco HQ moved to Redwood City. Route via Moloco PR (pr@moloco.com).

name: Elia Wallen
current_role: Founder and CEO, Engine (formerly Hotel Engine), Denver, Colorado
profile: Denver entrepreneur who founded corporate-housing firm Travelers Haven in 2008, then spun its hotel-booking side into Hotel Engine (independent in 2018). Rebranded Engine in 2024 after a Series C (~$140M), it now books hotels, flights and cars for businesses and is valued around $2B. Wallen left the Travelers Haven CEO role in 2020 to run Engine full time.
interesting_fact: Engine grew out of Travelers Haven customers asking for help booking hotels; Wallen was named ColoradoBiz Magazine's CEO of the Year in December 2024.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2017, long before the unicorn round, EY named Wallen an Entrepreneur Of The Year award winner (hospitality, Mountain Desert region) at a gala at the Denver Center for the Performing Arts; Travelers Haven had placed 20,000+ traveling professionals in 2016 alone.
notes: Writes occasional Inc. columns (e.g., Nov 2025) on company-building lessons. Engine press room is the best route.

name: Jett McCandless
current_role: Founder and CEO, project44 (Chicago); also Founder and CEO of LSP44
profile: Logistics-tech veteran with 25+ years in freight; built GlobalTranz and Inc. 500-ranked Metafora before founding supply-chain visibility platform project44 in Chicago in 2014. project44 (valued ~$3B) is used by 500+ Global 200 brands; he also leads spin-off LSP44 for logistics providers and is a frequent Bloomberg TV voice on supply chains.
interesting_fact: project44's company bio says he has advised the White House Council of Economic Advisers and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on supply chains.
deep_cut_fact: He founded Blue Water Companies, a diversified portfolio company through which he pursues philanthropy and sustainability, including directing a significant portion of his personal net worth to organizations supporting women in crisis.
notes: Media-friendly (Bloomberg TV regular). press@project44.com appears in a 2025 republished release per search but not directly verified; LSP44 uses press@lsp44.ai.

name: Thibaud Elziere
current_role: Co-founder of Hexa (formerly eFounders) startup studio; CEO of Folk (CRM built within Hexa)
profile: French serial entrepreneur (b. 1979, Aix-en-Provence) who co-founded stock-photo site Fotolia in 2004 (sold to Adobe in 2014 for ~EUR800M), then in 2011 co-founded startup studio eFounders (Hexa since 2022), which launched ~40 startups including unicorns Spendesk, Front and Aircall. He has run Folk since 2019 and has angel-invested in ~100 startups (Algolia, Notion, Hugging Face).
interesting_fact: Hexa's studio model hands founders a ready idea, seed funding and support; its startups (Spendesk, Front, Aircall) reached a combined ~$5B valuation and ~2,800 jobs.
deep_cut_fact: He started Fotolia while still a student at Ecole Centrale de Lyon, and his side ventures include Gama Space, a solar-sail space project, and Kate, a microcar maker.
notes: Spendesk's operating co-founder/CEO is Rodolphe Ardant; Elziere is co-founder via the eFounders studio. Based in Brussels. Gama Space solar sail could be a good energy/space hook.

name: Zheng Yong
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Geek+ (Beijing Geekplus Technology; HKEX: 2590)
profile: Tsinghua graduate who spent ~5 years at ABB and ~3 years as a plant manager at a Saint-Gobain subsidiary, then was a senior investment manager at New Horizon Capital before founding warehouse-robotics company Geek+ in Beijing in 2015. Geek+ listed in Hong Kong in July 2025 as the first global AMR warehouse-robot stock; he held ~38% pre-IPO.
interesting_fact: Geek+'s July 2025 HK IPO was the largest robotics H-share IPO to date; the retail tranche was ~134x oversubscribed and 2024 revenue was ~RMB2.4B, the largest of any HK-listed B2B robot maker.
deep_cut_fact: The idea came in 2014 while he was a VC at New Horizon Capital touring an Amazon warehouse full of Kiva robots; he couldn't find a Chinese team to back, so he founded one, starting with just himself and CTO Li Hongbo in a basement of Tsinghua's FIT building, and shipping its first goods-to-person product for Tmall's Singles' Day in under three months.
notes: Chinese name 郑勇. Public company, so IR/PR routes are formal and responsive. Quote: 'We enter each market not asking whether we can win, only how long until we're No.1 locally.'

name: Ofer Herman
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO of Papaya Global (2016-2023); current role not publicly confirmed
profile: Israeli technologist who co-founded global payroll and workforce-payments platform Papaya Global in 2016 with Eynat Guez and Ruben Drong, serving as CTO as it grew to a $3.7B valuation in its 2021 Series D. He announced in June 2023 that he was leaving Papaya after seven-plus years. Earlier he co-founded AASL and co-founded/led MRD-IT Solutions and SafelyGuard.
interesting_fact: Papaya Global went from a $1.5M seed in 2016 to a $3.7B valuation in Sept 2021 (Series D led by Insight Partners and Tiger Global), and later bought UK payments firm Azimo.
notes: Very low public profile; no current venture found after leaving Papaya in June 2023 (per aggregator citing his LinkedIn post). Earlier ventures (AASL, MRD-IT Solutions, SafelyGuard) from Welcome to the Jungle profile only. Best route likely LinkedIn.

name: Bo Chen
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Xendit (Southeast Asian payments infrastructure)
profile: UC Berkeley EECS graduate (2014) who briefly worked at Brandcast and Ripple before co-founding Xendit in 2015 with fellow Berkeley alum Moses Lo (plus Tessa Wijaya and Juan Gonzalez). Xendit builds payment rails across Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, and was valued at ~$3B after its 2022 Series D.
interesting_fact: Xendit was the first Indonesian tech startup accepted into Y Combinator (S15 batch) and the first B2B payments company in Indonesia to reach unicorn status; Chen founded it at 23.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated early from Berkeley to get into startups faster, and his official festival bio notes he likes creating original rap performances for Xendit company offsites; he spoke at Singapore FinTech Festival 2023 on 'Become a Cockroach: Survive to Thrive.'
notes: CEO Moses Lo is the main public face. Xendit press releases list PR staff contacts (e.g., Ami Windarti, PR & Communications; a 2022 Series D release listed ami@xendit.co) - not independently re-verified, check newest release on xendit.co newsroom.

name: Tiantian Kullander
current_role: Deceased (co-founder of Amber Group, Hong Kong crypto financial services firm)
profile: Co-founder of Hong Kong-based digital-asset firm Amber Group (2017), a former Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley trader. He died unexpectedly in his sleep on November 23, 2022, aged 30, per Amber Group.
notes: Died 23 Nov 2022 (source: The Block, citing Amber Group statement). Not a candidate for outreach.

name: Christina Cacioppo
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Vanta (security compliance automation)
profile: Midwest-raised founder who began her career in venture at Union Square Ventures, quit to teach herself to code, helped build Dropbox Paper, then founded Vanta in 2017 to automate SOC 2 and other security compliance. Vanta scaled to $10M ARR before raising a Series A and was valued around $4B by 2025.
interesting_fact: Vanta famously reached $10M ARR before raising a Series A; she has said she worked through many failed ideas ('I failed 22 times') before landing on compliance automation.
deep_cut_fact: Her personal site says her internet life began in the 90s on Beanie Baby forums and eBay, she 'still bleeds scarlet and gray,' loves 80s-90s gymnastics and Magritte's L'Empire des lumieres, and she angel-invested in Nigerian ISP Tizeti in 2017.
notes: Publishes her own email on her personal site - best direct route. Frequent podcast guest (Masters of Scale, My First Million, Invest Like the Best).

name: Peng Xiaobo
current_role: Chairman and General Manager (legal representative, controlling shareholder ~32%), Beijing Interstellar Glory Space Technology (iSpace)
profile: Rocket designer trained in aircraft design at Beihang University who leads iSpace, one of China's first private launch companies (founded 2016). In July 2019 its Hyperbola-1 became the first Chinese private rocket to reach orbit. He now steers the reusable LOX-methane Hyperbola-3, aimed at deploying China's mega LEO internet constellations; iSpace raised a Series D in 2025.
interesting_fact: iSpace's Hyperbola-1, launched 25 July 2019 from Jiuquan, made iSpace the first privately owned Chinese company to put a rocket into orbit.
deep_cut_fact: Born in the 1970s, he told Xinhua that as a child he found satellites and rockets 'magical' and wanted to understand them, so he chose aircraft design at Beihang for the gaokao; his roadmap for iSpace is 'solid to liquid, small to large, sky to ground.'
notes: Chinese name 彭小波. Some reports say he formally became iSpace GM in 2018 after a career at China Academy of Launch Vehicle Technology. No published press email found. Space/launch angle relevant to energy/data-center (LEO constellations).

name: Chris Park
current_role: Co-founder and VP of Engineering, Material Security (Redwood City, CA)
profile: UC Berkeley EECS graduate who worked on data privacy at Google, was the first engineer at Parastructure (acquired by Dropbox) and then led Dropbox infrastructure teams, before co-founding email and cloud-workspace security company Material Security in 2017 with Abhishek Agrawal and Ryan Noon. Material protects Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace and reached a ~$1B valuation.
interesting_fact: All three Material co-founders came out of Dropbox; the company was started in 2017 in the wake of the 2016 election email-hacking incidents, to protect sensitive data sitting in mailboxes.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Material he was the very first engineer at Parastructure, the startup co-founded by his future Material co-founder Ryan Noon, which Dropbox acquired; earlier he led data-privacy and authorization projects at Google.
notes: Engineering-focused, low public profile; CEO Abhishek Agrawal is the public face. No press email found on Material's site (disclosure@material.security exists but is for security reports). 'First engineer at Parastructure' is from profile aggregators; Material's page confirms Parastructure/Dropbox/Google.

name: Todd Mackey
current_role: Co-founder, President & COO, MightyByte (maker of the ClassCalc math calculator app)
profile: Southern California entrepreneur and angel investor (R. Todd Mackey) who co-founded web-filtering/classroom-management EdTech company GoGuardian, serving as President & COO 2014-2016 after leading its Series A; GoGuardian was acquired by Sumeru Equity Partners in 2018 and later valued ~$1B. He has since co-founded MightyByte, which builds the free ClassCalc calculator app for students.
interesting_fact: He says he has co-founded and/or scaled six companies across manufacturing, industrial products and education, with experience spanning investment banking to operations.
deep_cut_fact: On ClassCalc's team page he describes himself as a beach-loving volleyball player, world explorer and 'lover of dark chocolate and BF The Cookie,' and says education should be made cheap and accessible for all.
notes: Moved to advisory role at GoGuardian in Aug 2016 (self-reported). team@classcalc.com is a general company inbox. Social links are from his self-written (unverified) Wellfound profile.

name: Christof Roduner
current_role: Co-founder, CIO and VP Engineering, Scandit (Zurich)
profile: Swiss computer scientist and co-founder (2009, with Samuel Mueller and Christian Floerkemeier) of Scandit, the Zurich-based smart data capture company whose smartphone-camera barcode scanning and computer vision is used in retail and logistics; it reached unicorn status in 2022. He leads Scandit's software engineering and research organisation.
interesting_fact: Scandit grew out of ETH Zurich/MIT Internet-of-Things research, aiming to bridge physical objects and digital information just as smartphone cameras became capable enough.
deep_cut_fact: Before research he founded a company that built and sold a CRM system and ran the internet business at a Zurich IT firm; as an ETH/MIT researcher he co-founded Fosstrak, the leading open-source RFID platform implementing the EPC Network spec, used by SAP and Orange.
notes: Studied CS and business at University of Zurich and Uppsala. Appeared on Swisspreneur podcast ep. 249 (2022). Samuel Mueller (CEO) is the main public face.

name: Brett Shaheen
current_role: Founder and CEO, Redesign Health (New York healthcare venture studio)
profile: Former Lone Pine Capital partner and lead healthcare analyst (earlier Carlyle, Goldman Sachs, Google and BCG) who founded Redesign Health in 2018, a venture studio that co-founds, staffs and funds new healthcare companies from scratch. Redesign raised $175M in Dec 2024 and has been valued around $2B.
interesting_fact: Redesign Health builds companies from scratch rather than investing in existing ones, recruiting founder-CEOs to run startups it designs and capitalizes; it has launched dozens of companies.
deep_cut_fact: He studied at Christ Church, Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar (MPhil in International Relations), after graduating summa cum laude from Wharton/Penn, and later earned a Harvard MBA.
notes: Search results indicate a press office address press@redesignhealth.com and named comms contacts on Business Wire releases (e.g., Dec 2024 $175M release), but I could not re-verify them on-page; check redesignhealth.com/press.
